title: Microsoft Teams Rooms and shared devices: passwordless sign-in for Entra resource accounts
summary: The briefing passes: the migration paths, password-cleanup permissions and device prerequisites agree with Microsoft Learn. It accurately reports optional migration, the existing device licence requirements and the disagreement between the roadmap's cloud list and the resource-account management documentation.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Migration does not remove the resource-account password from Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: After a Teams device transitions to password-less authentication, its resource account password remains in Microsoft Entra ID, but the device no longer uses that password to sign in.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends cleanup or manual password rotation after migration.
claims.quote: We recommend that IT administrators use the cleanup steps or manually rotate the password after the transition to ensure that the password is unknown and secure.

claims.claim: The retained password remains an account credential until reset or rotated.
claims.quote: its resource account password remains in Microsoft Entra ID, but the device no longer uses that password to sign in. Reset or scramble the password to a complex, secure value that isn't known or retained by an administrator.

claims.claim: Authentication to Microsoft 365 services such as Teams, Intune and Pro Management does not change.
claims.quote: Authentication to Microsoft 365 services (Teams, Intune, Pro Management Portal, etc) does not change.

claims.claim: Microsoft lists removal of resource accounts from meeting chats after calls end as a benefit of Set as Resource.
claims.quote: Removes resource accounts from meeting chats after the call ends

claims.claim: An administrative-unit-scoped Password Administrator can reset only nonadministrator accounts within that unit.
claims.quote: An administrative unit-scoped Password Administrator can reset passwords only for nonadministrator accounts in that administrative unit.

claims.claim: Password Administrator might not reset accounts with an Entra administrative role or membership or ownership of a role-assignable group.
claims.quote: If the resource account has a Microsoft Entra administrative role, or is a member or owner of a role-assignable group, Password Administrator might not be able to reset its password.

claims.claim: Removing unnecessary privileged assignments or using an appropriate higher-privileged role is Microsoft's documented guidance.
claims.quote: Remove unnecessary privileged assignments from the resource account or use an appropriate higher-privileged role.

claims.claim: For synchronized Windows Server Active Directory accounts, password resets or scrambling ordinarily occur in the source directory.
claims.quote: For resource accounts synchronized from Windows Server Active Directory, reset or scramble the password in the source directory unless password writeback is enabled and the domain is managed.

claims.claim: Enabled password writeback with a managed domain is the documented exception to source-directory password resets.
claims.quote: reset or scramble the password in the source directory unless password writeback is enabled and the domain is managed.

claims.claim: Federated account passwords must be changed through their authoritative identity provider.
claims.quote: If authentication is federated to an external identity provider, change the password through that authoritative identity provider.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Governance guidance: After rollout

claims.claim: Only the authentication method changes; supported device functionality remains unchanged.
claims.quote: Only the authentication method changes. The device uses a secure, device-bound resource account credential instead of a stored username and password. Meeting, calling, device-management, and other supported device functionality remain unchanged.

claims.claim: Microsoft says end users notice no changes to device functionality.
claims.quote: End users notice no changes to the device functionality.

claims.quote: A reset of the Teams Rooms on Windows devices is required to revert from password-less authentication. A reset can be performed using the recovery image from your Teams Rooms manufacturer or with the recovery tool.

claims.claim: A full account sign-out removes the passwordless token on Android rooms, panels and phones.
claims.quote: Teams Rooms on Android, Teams panels, and Teams phones: A full account sign out on the device will remove the password-less authentication token and allow a new sign in with a username and password.

claims.quote: Crestron's unique software configuration is not currently compatible with password-less resource accounts.
